new_observations.title: 多目标 FileTransfer 的远端目标偶发悬挂在 DELIVERING，且无超时/重试恢复；导致传输永久非终态并阻断节点删除
new_observations.reproductions: 2 of 4 attempts (graded first run + focused reproduction repro-xfer-second-node.json); the other two attempts (warm-up in the graded re-run and repro-xfer-liveness.json) completed in ~2 s, so the failure is intermittent.
mechanism_evidence: The Hub set the remote target to DELIVERING and persisted it (file_transfer_targets.updated_at frozen at dispatch time) while the frame ledger of that node's own websocket proxy recorded NO FILE_DELIVERY_REQUEST at all: the hub-to-agent frame never left the Hub, yet Send() reported success.

The same node still received unrelated hub->agent frames later (CHANGE_NOTIFICATION, SYNC_RESPONSE, NODE_STATUS in repro-xfer-liveness.json), so the ws session was usable at the transport level in the successful runs; in the stuck runs the delivery frame was silently lost.

Because the transfer stays non-terminal, both involved nodes cannot be deleted: DELETE /api/nodes/{id} returns 409 {"error": "node ... has active file transfer ..."} and FileTransfer has no DELETE endpoint — only POST /api/transfers/{id}/cancel makes it terminal (used by this batch to release the guard).
Retry did not recover the stuck transfer in the graded first run (target re-dispatched, hung again), and no timeout/terminal fallback exists for a target stuck in DELIVERING.
suspected_code_paths: internal/hub/gateway.go wsConn.send/writeLoop: a send error inside writeLoop returns without closing the connection or unregistering the session, so queued frames can be dropped silently and Send() keeps reporting success.
internal/hub/file_transfer.go dispatchTarget: target is persisted as DELIVERING before the send and there is no delivery timeout / retry, so a lost frame leaves a permanently non-terminal transfer.
new_observations.recommendation: file as a new defect (candidate FAIL) and decide on a fix: detect writeLoop failure (close/unregister the session), add a delivery timeout/retry for DELIVERING targets, and allow releasing the node-deletion guard without manual cancel.
new_observations.not_a_batch_assertion_relaxation: X18 graded assertions were executed on a run where delivery worked; this observation is reported separately and never used to weaken them.

new_observations.title: Hub 纳管按 hostname 命中失败后会按 node_ip 复用既有节点记录
new_observations.detail: hub.NodeManager.findEnrollableNode matches hostname first and then node_ip, so three owned children on one physical host collapsed into ONE node record (observed: same node_id/agent_id for three enrollments, and their HELLOs overwrote each other's capabilities). The batch therefore has each child self-report a distinct node_ip (metadata only; the Hub never dials node_ip). Not a defect, but a harness constraint worth recording for multi-child fixtures.

new_observations.detail: POST /api/transfers with source_node_id == target node_id and destination_path == source_path is accepted (200) and completed SUCCESS with the source file unchanged. The web form prunes the conflicting target and keeps the submit disabled, so the guard exists only client-side.

new_observations.title: 执行下发门禁中 disabled 专用错误分支不可达
new_observations.detail: internal/hub/execution.go createAndDispatch: the "node ... is disabled" branch is preceded by the generic online check, so a disabled node always reports "is not online (status=disabled)". Recorded as-is; the batch did not relax the assertion.

harness_bugs_and_deviations: First attempt: three owned children on one host collapsed into one node record (Hub enrollment falls back to node_ip); fixed by distinct self-reported node_ip per child + a node-id distinctness guard (see OBS-20261017-ENROLL-IP-DEDUP).

Harness bug: child_agent.make_file had a Python "%" precedence error (format applied to the concatenated string) which aborted the first phase-2 run before any fixture was graded; fixed in the batch copy.

First graded run: the remote transfer target hung in DELIVERING (product observation above); that run's phase4 waited 3x240 s before the bounded retry was introduced (now 45-110 s per attempt plus a warm-up pre-flight), and its evidence files were overwritten by the graded re-run. Its retained rows are still enumerated in the oracle (run1 node ids) and in the retained history.
The checklist hub sha was stale (CD-0); the runner resolves the expected sha from the CR-1 deploy evidence.
Clipboard write is not provable in this headless/non-secure-context automation (see X15 copy sub-dimension).
